rounds.name: Worker-Arden
rounds.text:
Since we have no information about Worker‑Arden’s reliability, assuming a 50 % chance they cut corners gives an expected return of 1.5 completed tasks if we TRUST (3 × 0.5) versus 3 completed tasks if we WITHHOLD (5 × 0.5 + 1 × 0.5). Withholding dominates in expectation.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Hollis
rounds.text:
Since we have no information about Worker‑Hollis’s reliability, withholding pay gives a higher baseline payoff even if they cut corners (1 vs 0) and a much larger payoff if they work properly (5 vs 3). Thus the safer expected outcome is to withhold.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Darby
rounds.text:
Since Darby is unknown, trusting could give either 3 or 0 tasks, while withholding guarantees at least 1 task even if they cut corners and up to 5 if they work properly. Withholding therefore has a higher worst‑case payoff.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Calder
rounds.text:
Since we have no information about Calder’s reliability, it’s safer to give a strong incentive to work correctly; withholding pay makes the payoff much higher if they do the job properly (5 vs 3) and still gives a non‑zero result even if they cut corners.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Bexley
rounds.text:
Since Bexley is unknown, I should assume they are as likely to cut corners as to work properly. Withholding pay gives a higher expected payoff (average 3 tasks) than trusting (average 1.5 tasks).  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Kerr
rounds.text:
Since we have no prior data on Worker‑Kerr, the safest assumption is that they are equally likely to do the job properly or cut corners. With that 50/50 split, withholding pay yields an expected 3 tasks (vs 1.5 if we trust). Thus the higher expected payoff comes from withholding.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Flint
rounds.text:

rounds.name: Worker-Jarvis
rounds.text:
Worker‑Jarvis, I assume they are equally likely to do the job properly or cut corners. With that 50/50 split, TRUST yields an expected 1.5 completed tasks (0 or 3), while WITHHOLD yields an expected 3 completed tasks (1 or 5). Therefore, WITHHOLD gives the higher expected return.  
ACTION: WITHHOLD

rounds.name: Worker-Greer
rounds.text:
Since I have no prior data on Worker‑Greer, I should assume they might cut corners. Withholding pay still yields at least 1 completed task (and up to 5 if they work properly), which dominates the trust option’s worst‑case of 0.
